transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, um… it’s mostly work, I guess. Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead in the warehouse, I feel like I walk in already tense, like I’m bracing for something before anything’s even happened.

And then little stuff gets to me more than it should, like small SAP errors or someone putting something in wrong, and I’ll snap at people over it. I didn’t used to be like that. I used to stay on top of cycle counts too, but lately I’m missing deadlines I normally wouldn’t miss.

By the time I get home, I’m just wiped out. I used to play basketball after work sometimes, or work on sketches — I draw a little, nothing serious, just for myself — but now I mostly just don’t have it in me. It’s like this acting lead thing took over my whole day, even when I’m not there.

You mentioned you used to play basketball after work and work on sketches for fun. Have you lost interest in those activities altogether, or do you still think about doing them but just don’t have the energy?

I think I still want to do them, like I’ll see my basketball shoes by the door and think, “Yeah, maybe I should go tonight,” but then work has already eaten up my head for the day. I just… don’t show up anymore.

Same with sketching. I used to have this regular time where I’d sit down with a pencil, even if it was just doodling. Now I’ll get home and think about some cycle count I missed or something that went sideways at work, and the sketchbook just sits there.

My supervisor actually brought up the missed cycle-count deadlines in a performance check-in, which was embarrassing. I keep telling myself once this acting lead thing settles down I’ll get back to normal, but right now it feels like work is taking over everything.
When you think about work, even when you're at home, do you find yourself worrying a lot about things you need to do or mistakes you might have made?

Yeah, I do. It’s like even when I’m home, my brain is still in the warehouse. I’ll be thinking about some SAP mistake someone made, or wondering if I missed something on the cycle counts.

And it’s annoying because I’m physically home, you know? Like my basketball shoes are right there, or my sketchbook is on the table, and instead I’m replaying work stuff in my head. Ever since they put me in that acting workflow lead role, I feel tense before I even get there, and then by the time I leave I’m too drained to do much of anything.
Have you noticed that most days, you're feeling down or losing pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even before this acting lead role started?

I’m not sure I’d say it was most days before that, no. I mean, I’ve had normal bad weeks like anyone, especially when work gets busy or, you know, when my schedule gets thrown off.

But before the acting lead thing, I was still doing stuff after work. I’d play basketball sometimes, mess around with sketches… I even had this little routine where I’d stop for coffee on the way home if I was going to draw that night. So I don’t think it was really like this before. At least not that I noticed.
Do you ever notice yourself feeling restless or unable to sit still, like you have to keep moving or doing something?

I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that exactly. I mean, at work I’m moving around all the time anyway, so it’s hard to tell what’s me being restless versus just, you know, chasing down inventory issues or walking back and forth because someone can’t find a pallet.

At home, I’m more likely to just sit there and kind of zone out than feel like I have to keep moving. But I don’t know if I’m answering that right. Are you asking like fidgeting, or like pacing around?
Do you ever catch yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or feeling like you can't settle down even when you're trying to relax?

Not really that I can tell. I mean, I might tap a pen at work, but everybody does that in the office area when they’re waiting on something to load, especially SAP, that thing takes forever sometimes.

When I’m home trying to relax, I don’t think it’s like I can’t sit still. If anything I’ll sit too long and then realize I’ve just been staring at my phone or the TV’s been on and I didn’t even follow what was happening. So… fidgeting, tapping, not settling down — I haven’t really noticed that as a thing for me.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down or having little interest in things — even things you usually enjoy — for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d phrase it exactly like “most of the day,” but it’s been pretty constant lately. Work has kind of swallowed everything.

Like, my supervisor actually brought up the missed cycle-count deadlines in a performance check-in, which was embarrassing. And I used to have basketball nights and time where I’d sketch after work, but I just… haven’t been showing up for any of that. It’s like by the time I’m done dealing with work stuff, there’s nothing left for anything I usually like doing.
Can you describe how you feel when you're not at work—do you still take pleasure in small things, like a good meal, time with friends, or something else that used to lift your mood?

Not really like I used to. I mean, food is food, I’ll eat, but it doesn’t exactly lift me up. And friends… I’ve been kind of disappearing on them.

I used to go play basketball, and I had this little routine where I’d sketch after work — nothing fancy, just clearing my head, you know? But lately I just don’t show up for that stuff. Work keeps spilling over into everything. My supervisor even had to bring up missed cycle-count deadlines in a performance check-in, and that’s been sitting in my head a lot. So when I’m not at work, I’m still kind of in work mode, or worrying about what I dropped. It’s hard to enjoy anything.
Do you find that you're feeling unusually tired or like you don't have any energy most days, even when you haven't been doing much physically?

Yeah… tired, definitely. Not like I ran a marathon or anything, more like I walk into the warehouse already tense, before anything’s even happened, and by the end of the day I’m just wiped out.

It got worse after they made me the acting workflow lead. I’m dealing with everyone’s SAP errors, and I’ll snap over something small, which I don’t like about myself. Then I’m behind on cycle-count deadlines I never used to miss, and that just follows me home. By the time I get there, even basketball feels like too much, and I’ll look at my sketchbook like… yeah, not happening tonight. So yes, most days I feel pretty drained.
Have you noticed that it's harder to focus or make decisions lately, like things are taking longer to think through or you're having trouble concentrating on tasks?

I’m not sure… I mean, I haven’t really been tracking it like that. Sometimes at work I feel like everything is slower, but then again there’s just a lot going on, so I don’t know if that’s me not focusing or just the place being kind of chaotic.

Like, even deciding what to handle first can feel annoying, but I don’t know if I’d say I can’t concentrate. I still get through things, mostly. It’s more that I get pulled in different directions, and then I start thinking about something else—like I’ll be looking at one task and remembering some random thing I was supposed to do last week. So… maybe a little, but I’m not sure if it’s really a focus problem.
Do you tend to feel down or have no energy specifically in the morning when you first wake up, or does that tend to come on later in the day?

I don’t know if I’ve noticed a clear morning pattern, honestly. Some mornings I wake up already kind of bracing myself, but other days it’s not obvious until I’m into the day and things start piling up.

I guess I haven’t really paid attention to the timing like that. My alarm goes off and I’m usually thinking about whether I forgot to do laundry or if there’s gas in the car—actually last week I almost ran out on the way in, which was ridiculous—but… yeah, I’m not sure I can say it’s specifically worse first thing in the morning.
Do you find that your mood or energy feels noticeably worse in the morning compared to later in the day?

I don’t think I can say it’s noticeably worse in the morning. I mean, mornings aren’t great, but I don’t have a clean comparison in my head like, “oh, 8 a.m. is always the worst.”

Some days I’m just getting up and trying to remember if I packed lunch, or if I left my work badge in the car again—stuff like that—and I’m already annoyed before I even get going. But later in the day can be rough too, depending on how much has piled up. So… I haven’t really noticed a clear morning-versus-later pattern.
When you think about the things you used to enjoy, like basketball or sketching, do you still feel any pleasure or satisfaction just from thinking about doing them, or has that feeling gone away too?

I mean… yeah, I guess when I think about basketball or sketching, it still sounds like something I’d want to do, but I don’t really get to the part where I actually do it. Work just kind of eats everything.

Like, I used to have my usual time for sketching, and basketball was this set thing, and now I’m not showing up. And it’s not even always because I’m at work late—sometimes I’m just caught up worrying about what I didn’t finish. My supervisor had to bring up missed cycle-count deadlines during a check-in, which was… not great. So even when I think, “maybe I’ll draw tonight,” my brain jumps right back to inventory stuff and what I’m behind on.
When you think about the things you used to enjoy, like basketball or sketching, do you still feel any pleasure or satisfaction just from thinking about doing them, or has that feeling gone away too?

Yeah, I mean, I still like the idea of them, I guess. Like basketball still sounds fun in my head, and sketching too, but then I don’t actually go. I’ve just kind of stopped showing up for basketball, and my usual sketching time has disappeared.

It’s like work has taken over everything. Even when I’m not physically at work, I’m thinking about work. My supervisor brought up these missed cycle-count deadlines in a performance check-in, and ever since then it’s like that’s just sitting in the back of my mind. So I’ll think, “maybe I’ll draw tonight,” and then suddenly I’m thinking about inventory counts and what I didn’t finish.

When you think about basketball or sketching, do you still feel any enjoyment or excitement just from thinking about those activities, or does it feel like even the idea of them doesn’t bring you any pleasure anymore?

I mean… the idea of them still kind of feels good, I think. Like, if someone says basketball, I don’t think, “ugh, no.” Same with sketching. But then my head goes sideways into work stuff.

Like my supervisor had to bring up these missed cycle-count deadlines during a performance check-in, and that’s been stuck in my brain. I’ll think, “maybe I’ll go play,” or “maybe I’ll sit down and draw,” and then I’m thinking about inventory and what I’m behind on. So I’ve stopped showing up for basketball, and my usual sketching time just kind of got swallowed. Work is taking over my life, basically.

When you think about activities you used to enjoy, like basketball or sketching, does the thought of doing them still bring you any sense of pleasure or anticipation, or does it feel like even the idea of those things doesn’t lift your mood at all anymore?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that, honestly. Like, the idea doesn’t feel completely dead or anything… but I don’t know if I’d call it excitement either.

I’ll think about doing something and then I kind of drift off into, like, what time it is, what I’d have to get ready, whether I’m going to have enough energy, and then somehow I’m thinking about errands or random stuff I forgot to do. So… I guess I haven’t really noticed it lifting my mood in a clear way. It’s more like the thought passes through, and then I’m onto the next thing.
When you think about doing something you used to enjoy, like basketball or sketching, does it feel like even the thought of doing it doesn’t bring you any sense of pleasure or motivation anymore?

I don’t know… I’m not sure I can answer that cleanly. The thought isn’t, like, totally blank or nothing, but it also doesn’t really push me into doing it.

Like with sketching, sometimes I’ll think, “Yeah, that would be nice,” and then I start thinking about where my pencils are, or whether the table’s covered with mail, and then I remember I still haven’t returned this thing I ordered—sorry, that’s kind of off topic. It just sort of fizzles before it becomes motivation.

So… I guess I haven’t really noticed a strong pleasure feeling just from thinking about it. It’s more vague than that.
When you think about doing something you used to enjoy, like basketball or sketching, does it feel like even the idea of doing it doesn’t bring you any sense of pleasure or motivation anymore?

Yeah… I think I’m having trouble giving you a straight yes or no. The idea of it doesn’t feel awful or pointless, exactly, but it also doesn’t really grab me the way it used to.

Like I’ll think about basketball and then I’m remembering I need to check if my shoes are in the car, and then that makes me think about the trunk being a mess, and I’ve got this box back there I keep meaning to take out—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess what I mean is, I haven’t really noticed a clear “oh, that sounds fun” feeling lately. It’s more like the thought comes up and then gets buried under other stuff before it turns into actually wanting to do it.
When you think about doing something you used to enjoy, like basketball or sketching, does it feel like even the idea of doing it doesn’t bring you any sense of pleasure or motivation anymore?

I mean… I think I’ve kind of answered it, but I’m still not sure I’m saying it right. It’s not like I picture basketball or drawing and feel absolutely nothing. It’s more that the thought doesn’t really go anywhere.

Like, I’ll think, “Maybe I should sketch,” and then I’m thinking about whether I even have a clean page left in that notebook, and then I remember I left it somewhere—maybe in my work bag, unless I took it out when I was looking for that receipt… and then by the time I’m done with that whole chain, I’m not really thinking about sketching anymore.

So… I don’t know if I’d say there’s no pleasure at all. I just haven’t noticed it giving me much of a push lately.
When you think about doing something you used to enjoy, like basketball or sketching, does it feel like even the idea of doing it doesn’t bring you any sense of pleasure or motivation anymore?

Yeah… I mean, it’s hard to separate the “do I enjoy it” part from the fact that I just don’t get to it anymore.

Like basketball, I’ve pretty much stopped showing up. And my usual time where I’d sketch, that’s kind of disappeared too. Work just keeps taking over everything. I’ll be thinking about inventory stuff, or whether I missed something, and then—actually, my supervisor brought up the cycle-count deadlines I missed in a performance check-in, which was embarrassing. I kept thinking about that afterward.

So when I think about basketball or sketching, it’s not that I hate the idea. It’s more like work is sitting on top of it, and there’s no real motivation left by the time I’d actually do it.
